title: The Waters Recede and Noah Leaves the Ark

verses.1: God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth, and the waters began to go down.
verses.2: The underground springs and the floodgates of the sky were closed, and the rain stopped falling.
verses.3: The waters continued to go down steadily. After 150 days the waters had decreased.
verses.4: In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
verses.5: The waters continued to decrease until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains could be seen.
verses.6: After forty days Noah opened the window of the ark he had made
verses.7: and sent out a raven. The raven flew back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
verses.8: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had gone down from the surface of the ground.
verses.9: But the dove could find no place to land because there was still water over all the earth. So it flew back to Noah in the ark. He reached out his hand and brought it back inside.
verses.10: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out from the ark again.
verses.11: The dove came back to him in the evening with a freshly picked olive leaf in its beak. Noah knew from this that the waters had gone down from the earth.
verses.12: He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, and this time it did not come back.
verses.13: In Noah's six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the water had dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and saw that the ground was dry.
verses.14: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry.
verses.16: "Come out of the ark — you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives.
verses.17: Bring out every living creature that is with you — the birds, the animals, and every creature that crawls on the ground — so they can spread over the earth and be fruitful and multiply."
verses.18: So Noah came out, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
verses.19: Every animal, every crawling creature, and every bird — everything that moves on the earth — came out of the ark, each according to its kind.
verses.20: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every kind of clean animal and clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.
verses.21: The LORD smelled the pleasing offering and said in His heart, "I will never again curse the ground because of people, even though their hearts are set on evil from childhood. I will never again destroy every living creature as I have done.
verses.22: As long as the earth remains, there will always be planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night."

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
